agree.reason: The speaker is a long-time Alder Road resident who names the traffic cost and accepts it, which gives the traffic-focused commissioners a reason to vote yes, though opposed neighbours will hear a church member asking them to bear a cost they didn't choose.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief, but calling it "the county's study" assigns an author the brief doesn't name, "spread across the whole day" plays down the rush-hour effect, and "chances like that don't come along often" is asserted without support.

works_the_facts.reason: The speech works out about five trips per unit (310/64), eight spare parking spaces (72 minus 64) and about one in six of the waiting list (64/412), all correct and well framed, though it never weighs 64 homes against the 2,100 shortfall or the three-year wait beyond restating them.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is fairly described as an empty lot six days a week and families still waiting, but the brief gives no trend, and the speech doesn't say whether the waiting list or the shortage is growing.

qualification.reason: The speech makes no conditional claims needing a hedge, and its one concession (64 won't close 2,100) is stated plainly.

objections.reason: The traffic objection is met head-on with the C-to-D drop admitted and the cost owned, but parking is raised when the 72-space fact already answers it and nobody in the reader description pressed it.

fit.reason: At about 400 words of short spoken lines with placeholders for names, it fits a three-minute public comment.
